LESSON: NUMBERS IN FRENCH BRAILLE • 1-10

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: French Braille 9.1 French Accent marks in Braille • Diphthon gs (Aeoe) (2 lesson
Topic 9.2: Numbers in French Braille • 1-10
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Numbers in French Braille • 1-10, part of French Braille 9.1 French Accent marks in Braille • Diphthon gs (Aeoe) (2 lesson in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is learning numbers in French Braille important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore Braille number symbols (1–10) using Braille cards with raised dots and corresponding French audio (“un,” “deux,) played by the teacher and discuss,

2. take turns in tactile reading of short number sequences (1–5 then 6–10) through guided finger movement and repetition and exchange with peers for correction,

3. use a Braille slate and stylus, refreshable Braille displays or Perkins Braille to write numbers 1–10 with correct use of the numeric prefix,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explore Braille number symbols (1–10) using Braille cards with raised dots and corresponding French audio (“un,” “deux,) played by the teacher and discuss,
2. take turns in tactile reading of short number sequences (1–5 then 6–10) through guided finger movement and repetition and exchange with peers for correction,
3. use a Braille slate and stylus, refreshable Braille displays or Perkins Braille to write numbers 1–10 with correct use of the numeric prefix,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Numbers in French Braille • 1-10 together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: the learners use refreshable Braille displays to write numbers with correct use of the numeric prefix.

● Communication and collaboration: the learners take turns in tactile reading of short number sequences through guided

finger movement and repetition.
